issues.t: Lower steering shaft joint may separate (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing before it happens. If the joint comes apart, the steering wheel stops turning the front wheels and you can lose steering control.
issues.why: On some 2017 QX30s the hole in the lower steering shaft that holds a universal-joint bearing allows too much movement, and the bearing can work loose and separate. NHTSA campaign 21V-419 covers these vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away. The dealer replaces the lower steering shaft for free. If the steering feels loose, notchy or binds, stop driving and have it towed. One owner reported the steering binding and wheel buttons failing after the recall work, so go back to the dealer promptly if anything feels different afterward.

issues.t: Driver airbag may go off unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning, though a broken clock spring often brings on the airbag light first. In rare cases the driver airbag can inflate without a crash.
issues.why: Parts of the steering system were not grounded well enough. If the clock spring (the coiled wiring ribbon behind the steering wheel) is broken, a static electricity discharge can set off the driver airbag. NHTSA campaign 17V-691 covers 2017-2018 QX30s.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for this recall and book it. The dealer adds grounding to the steering parts for free. If the airbag light is on, get it checked before long drives.

issues.t: Clicking steering wheel, airbag light and dead wheel buttons
issues.sym: A clicking or ticking from the steering wheel as you turn it, the airbag light and other warning lights coming on, and the horn or steering-wheel buttons stopping working.
issues.why: The clock spring, a coiled ribbon cable behind the steering wheel that carries power to the airbag, horn and buttons, can break. Infiniti ran a campaign (PG7BS) on the clock spring cable and steering column bushing for these cars, and owners still report failures outside the recall.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon, because the driver airbag may not work while this light is on. Ask the dealer whether your VIN has an open campaign or goodwill help before paying for the part.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may not inflate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning to the driver. In a crash the passenger front airbag might not inflate.
issues.why: The igniter inside the passenger airbag inflator may fail. It affects QX30s built between August 11 and September 27, 2016 (NHTSA campaign 16V-939).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the passenger airbag module free of charge.

issues.t: Driver-side curtain airbag may not inflate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning to the driver. In a side crash the left curtain airbag might not inflate.
issues.why: The inflator igniter in the driver-side curtain airbag may not fire. NHTSA campaign 17V-143 covers a small number of 2017 QX30s.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the driver-side curtain airbag free of charge.

issues.t: Right rear seat belt anchor may come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see. In a crash the lower anchor of the right-side seat belt could pull out.
issues.why: A bolt on the right-side lower seat belt anchor may not have been installed correctly at the factory. NHTSA campaign 18V-355 covers a handful of 2018 QX30s.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer welds in a retaining plate and fits a new anchor bolt for free.

issues.t: Backup camera picture can disappear (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera screen stays blank or shows no picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: The camera display settings could be changed so the image is effectively hidden, and the setting stays that way. NHTSA campaign 19V-654 covers many Nissan and Infiniti models, including 2018-2019 QX30s.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the free software update done. Until then, check the screen settings and look over your shoulder and in the mirrors when backing up.

issues.t: Jerky or hesitant shifts at low speed
issues.sym: Hesitation when pulling away, a lurch or bang on the 1-2 shift, shudder in stop-and-go traffic, or revs flaring before the car moves, often worst when cold.
issues.why: The QX30 shares its 7-speed dual-clutch automatic with the Mercedes GLA. These gearboxes are known for rough low-speed engagement as clutch adaptations drift, the fluid ages or the clutch packs wear. Mercedes dealers address it with software, a clutch relearn and, in some cases, a new clutch pack.
issues.next: Ask an Infiniti dealer to check for software updates and run a clutch adaptation reset. If the shudder or slipping gets worse, get a transmission diagnosis before the clutches are damaged further. Regular fluid changes help, despite "lifetime fill" claims.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A short rattle or chain-slap from the front of the engine for a few seconds after a cold start. It may come with a check engine light for camshaft timing codes.
issues.why: The 2.0L turbo comes from Mercedes (the M270 family). Its hydraulic chain tensioner can bleed down overnight, and the chain stretches faster when oil changes are stretched out or the oil is low.
issues.next: If the rattle lasts more than a couple of seconds or a check engine light appears, have it inspected soon; a jumped chain can wreck the engine. Use the specified oil and keep oil changes on time.

issues.t: Coolant leak or thermostat failure
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping, a coolant smell, the temperature gauge moving up or down, an overheating warning, or a weak heater.
issues.why: Owners report coolant leaks on the QX30. The Mercedes-sourced 2.0L turbo uses an electronically controlled thermostat and plastic coolant parts that wear and crack with heat, and the water pump can also fail.
issues.next: If the temperature warning comes on, pull over and turn the engine off. Do not open a hot coolant cap. Get the leak found soon; RepairPal lists thermostat replacement on the QX30 as a costly job.

issues.t: Oil leak from the turbo oil line
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the car, a burning-oil smell after driving, or oil residue around the turbocharger.
issues.why: An owner reported oil leaking from a turbocharger oil line on a QX30. The line seals and fittings near the hot turbo can harden and seep with age.
issues.next: Check the oil level and top it up if needed. Have the leak located soon, because oil dripping onto the hot exhaust can smoke or catch fire, and a turbo starved of oil fails quickly.

issues.t: Rough running and check engine light
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfire or loss of power, with the check engine light on.
issues.why: Owners report rough running with a check engine light, sometimes traced to the crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve. On this direct-injection engine, carbon also builds up on the intake valves over time and causes misfires and rough idle.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A failing PCV valve or ignition coil is a cheaper fix; heavy carbon buildup needs a walnut-blast cleaning. If the light flashes, slow down and get it checked right away.

issues.t: Start-stop (Eco) system stops working
issues.sym: The engine no longer shuts off at stops, or the Eco start-stop indicator shows a fault.
issues.why: Owners report the QX30's Eco start-stop system malfunctioning. The system turns itself off when it sees a weak 12-volt battery or a sensor fault.
issues.next: This is not a safety problem. Have the 12-volt battery tested first, since a tired battery is the most common reason start-stop quits.

issues.t: Navigation or infotainment screen freezes or goes blank
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, reboots, goes black or the navigation stops working.
issues.why: Infiniti has issued several bulletins for the QX30, including display control unit replacement (ITB13-026) and infotainment software updates (ITB23-010), and owners report navigation monitor faults.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for software updates first. If the screen is dead, a display control unit may need to be replaced. Your backup camera may not show while the screen is out, so take extra care in reverse.

issues.t: Rear headliner sags and blocks the rear window
issues.sym: The headliner fabric near the back drops down, sometimes when you open the sunroof shade, and hangs into the view through the rear window.
issues.why: The headliner at the rear of the cabin can come loose from its backing. Several owners have reported it to NHTSA, and one said Infiniti offered partial coverage.
issues.next: Pin or tape it up as a short-term fix so you can see out the back. Contact Infiniti Consumer Affairs and ask about goodwill coverage, then have the headliner reattached or replaced.

issues.t: Check engine light for small EVAP leak (P0456)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0456 and no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB17-042 says a leaking O-ring at the vent control valve of the fuel vapor (EVAP) system sets this code on the QX30.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight. If the light returns, ask the dealer to apply the bulletin; it is not urgent but the car may fail an emissions test.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking fails or shows a fault
issues.sym: A message that emergency braking is not working, or the system not braking or warning as expected before a collision.
issues.why: Owners have reported the forward emergency braking system not reacting or showing an "inoperative" warning, sometimes along with other electrical faults. The front radar sensor can be blocked by dirt or knocked out of alignment, and wiring faults can disable it.
issues.next: Never rely on the system to stop the car. Keep the front sensor area clean, and if the warning stays on, have the dealer check the radar, wiring and software.

issues.t: Front brakes noisy
issues.sym: Intermittent squeal or grinding from the front brakes, even on a newer car.
issues.why: An owner reported noisy front brakes on a 2019 QX30. Pad material, glazing or light rust on the rotors are common causes.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors checked. If the pads are worn down to metal, replace them right away.

issues.t: Clock resets every time the car starts
issues.sym: The dashboard clock goes back to a default time each time you turn the car on.
issues.why: Infiniti issued bulletin ITB19-039 for 2019 QX30s where the clock resets after each ignition cycle.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to apply the bulletin. It is a nuisance, not a safety issue.

issues.t: Seat leather wears through early
issues.sym: The leather on the seats cracks, scuffs or wears off at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners report the seat leather wearing through, around 11,000 miles on average, on 2018 QX30s.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about warranty or goodwill if the car is young. Leather conditioner slows wear; a re-dye or new seat cover is the fix.
